claims.head: The Bruins will hunt a mismatch
claims.call: The Bruins’ L2 (Peterka, Khusnutdinov and Minten) spends at least 41% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flyers’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Bruins have sent Peterka’s line (Peterka, Khusnutdinov and Minten) out against opponents’ third lines 41% of the time, when no line matching would give about 27%. That’s Marco Sturm chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Flyers’ third line is Bunting, Acciari and Cates.

claims.head: In close against from distance
claims.body: On shots from in close, Philadelphia ranks 16th in the league and Boston ranks 29th. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.call: The Flyers take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Bruins.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 5 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 53%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

C. McAvoy has not played this season. M. Lohrei is in his usual spot beside J. Aspirot, up from third-pair minutes last season. That pair is getting 15:08 a game at 5-on-5, up from 12:59 with McAvoy. W. Borgen has moved into Lohrei’s old spot beside H. Lindholm.

BOS.head: Nothing to separate these two
BOS.body: Philadelphia has had more of the chances over recent games and Boston has home ice. Boston can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

PHI.head: A genuine toss-up
PHI.body: Philadelphia has had more of the chances over recent games and Boston has home ice. For Philadelphia, the difference could be a power play that gets going.
